Please proofread this creative brief and flag anything vague.

CREATIVE BRIEF - Café Ombrelle, autumn range

Background
Café Ombrelle started as three neighbourhood coffee shops and is now moving into supermarket shelves with a range of ground coffee and pods. Awareness outside the home city is close to zero. Shelf competition is brutal and mostly fought on price promotions.

The problem
People who have never visited the shops see just another premium coffee pack. We need them to feel the warmth of the café before they have ever been inside one.

Audience
Urban 28-45, already buying premium coffee, curious, shops mostly online for groceries, sceptical of "artisan" claims.

What we want them to think
"This tastes like the good café round the corner, not like a factory."

Reasons to believe
- roasted in small batches in the original shop's roastery
- same baristas design every blend
- pods are home-compostable

Mandatories
Logo lockup, packshot of the full range, compostable icon.

Deliverables
KV + 3 OOH adapts, 6 social cutdowns (6s and 15s), retail shelf wobbler.

Timing
Routes in 2 weeks, tissue session before that. Launch window early October.

text:
Help me tighten the intro of our credentials deck. It's too long and a bit self-congratulatory.

"Studio Maréchal is an independent creative agency founded in Lyon, with a second studio in Paris. We believe that brands grow when they are brave enough to say something true. Like the teams behind Dove's Real Beauty or Share a Coke, we start from a human insight rather than a product feature. Our planners, writers, designers and film-makers work in one room, not in silos, which means ideas move fast from strategy to screen.

We work with challenger brands in food and drink, retail, travel and financial services. Some of our partnerships are confidential, so in this document they appear as Client A, Client B and so on, and the campaigns as Project [NAME]. What we can say is that most of our clients have been with us for more than four years, and that three of our last five campaigns were shortlisted at D&AD.

We don't do spec work, and we don't hide junior teams behind senior pitch teams. The people you meet at the chemistry meeting are the people who will work on your business. Think of us less like a supplier and more like the moonshot team inside your marketing department: the ones who get to try the Project Titan-style ideas that nobody else has time for, and then make them practical enough to run on a Monday morning."
note: Long negative: agency's own name, placeholders, public campaigns and a public codename, no client.
